title: Thin Soft Lavash
summary: Paper-thin, soft and pale flatbreads cooked for seconds on a very hot surface until blistered, then stacked under a towel to stay pliable.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
baking steel, stone or heavy griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix and knead
steps.text: Whisk the flour and yeast together, then add the honey, olive oil, salt and warm water at about 30 °C and mix to a soft dough. Knead for 6-8 minutes until smooth and only a little sticky. The small amount of oil keeps the finished breads soft and easy to fold.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover and leave for 45 minutes at room temperature. The dough will relax and puff a little rather than double, which is all it needs, since lavash wants tenderness rather than a big rise.

steps.title: Divide and relax
steps.text: Tip the dough out and divide it into 6 pieces of about 95 g. Shape into smooth rounds, cover loosely and rest for 20-30 minutes. Fully relaxed dough rolls out paper-thin without springing back.

steps.title: Heat the surface
steps.text: For the oven, place a baking steel or stone on a high shelf and heat the oven to its highest setting for at least 30 minutes; for the hob, heat a heavy griddle over high heat until very hot. Intense heat turns the water in the thin dough to steam instantly, puffing it before it can dry out.

steps.title: Roll very thin
steps.text: On a lightly floured surface, roll one piece at a time into an oval about 25 × 18 cm, so thin you can almost see through it. Brush off any excess flour, which would otherwise scorch and taste bitter.

steps.title: Cook in seconds
steps.text: Cook each sheet for about 20-30 seconds a side on the very hot surface, or close under a hot grill (broiler) if using the steel or stone, until it puffs with small blisters and is only lightly spotted. Stop while it is still pale; longer cooking makes it crisp rather than soft.

steps.title: Stack under a towel
steps.text: Stack each lavash under a clean tea towel as it comes off the heat, then roll and cook the rest. The trapped steam keeps the whole stack soft and foldable.

tips: The most common mistake is a surface that is not hot enough, which dries the bread before it puffs; give the steel or griddle the full heating time.
Roll one sheet while the previous one cooks to keep a steady rhythm.
If the dough keeps springing back, cover it and wait 5 minutes more before rolling again.
Lightly spritz a lavash that has dried out with water and warm it for a few seconds to soften it again.
storage: Keep the stacked lavash wrapped or in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Warm briefly in a dry pan or wrapped in foil in a low oven to soften. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
